criteria.title: Encrypted notifications fail locally when discovery does not advertise encrypted request support
criteria.assertion: When notification operations are invoked and current system discovery does not advertise both `nostr.service_pubkey` and at least one `nostr.browser_relays` value, the notifications store rejects locally before publish and does not call `requestEncryptedResult`.
preconditions: The requester is using the browser notifications store.
`encryptedRequestsAvailable(info)` returns false for current or lazily loaded Nostr discovery.
steps: Invoke `listNotificationChannels()` or `listNotificationLogs()` from the notifications store.
Observe store-side availability checks before any transport publish call.
criteria.expected_result: The operation throws an availability error, no encrypted request is published, and the corresponding store error field is populated.
negative_cases: If the store proceeds to `requestEncryptedResult` when encrypted discovery is unavailable, the criterion fails.
If the store leaves stale channel or log data in place after an availability failure, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: Notifications list route renders an error state when channel loading fails.
Store error fields contain the availability message.

criteria.title: Encrypted relay discovery uses the shared Bahia relay set with explicit capability gating
criteria.assertion: Encrypted notification transport derives relay URLs from `nostr.browser_relays`, but must become available only when discovery also advertises `nostr.service_pubkey` and `features.encrypted_nostr_requests`.
preconditions: System discovery contains `nostr.service_pubkey`.
System discovery may contain `browser_relays`, `service_pubkey`, and `features.encrypted_nostr_requests`.
steps: Resolve encrypted relay URLs from Nostr discovery.
Build or execute an encrypted notification request.
criteria.expected_result: Only URLs advertised in `browser_relays` are used for encrypted publish and result subscription, and encrypted transport stays unavailable unless the service pubkey and encrypted feature flag are present.
negative_cases: If a relay URL outside `browser_relays` is selected for encrypted request/result transport, the criterion fails.
If encrypted availability becomes true with only `browser_relays` present and no service pubkey/feature flag, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Encrypted notification requests are addressed to the Bahia service pubkey with the canonical wire marker
criteria.assertion: Each encrypted notification request is published as gift-wrapped ContextVM outer kind `1059`, addressed to the Bahia service pubkey with `['p', service_pubkey]`; the opaque inner request remains canonical ContextVM kind `25910` with the `['encrypted', 'contextvm-jsonrpc-v1']` routing marker.
preconditions: The browser signer is authenticated.
The encrypted transport has a valid 64-character service pubkey and at least one encrypted relay URL.
steps: Build an encrypted request event for a notification operation such as `notifications.channels.list`.
Inspect the signed inner event and the gift-wrapped outer event before publish.
criteria.expected_result: The outer request event carries kind `1059`, targets the service pubkey, contains opaque ciphertext rather than plaintext JSON, and wraps an inner signed ContextVM kind `25910` event with the canonical encrypted routing tag.
negative_cases: If the request omits the `p` tag for the Bahia service pubkey, the criterion fails.
If the request omits the encrypted routing tag or leaks plaintext content, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Encrypted publish success requires at least one accepted OK response
criteria.assertion: Publishing an encrypted notification request succeeds only when at least one encrypted relay returns `accepted=true`; when all relays reject, the caller receives the aggregated rejection reason.
preconditions: An encrypted notification request event has been built.
At least one encrypted relay connection is available to the transport client.
steps: Publish the encrypted request through the transport client.
Observe relay OK responses.
criteria.expected_result: The publish path returns success only with at least one accepted OK and returns an error containing relay rejection details when every OK is rejected.
negative_cases: If the transport treats `accepted=false` as success, the criterion fails.
If relay rejection reasons are discarded when all relays reject, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: Page-level notification actions surface the backend or relay error to the user via inline error or toast.

criteria.title: Encrypted notification results are correlated by request id, requester pubkey, and service author
criteria.assertion: The encrypted transport resolves a notification request only from an encrypted result event whose tags contain both the originating request event id and requester pubkey; unwrapped ContextVM results must also match the Bahia service author, and gift-wrapped results must validate the decrypted inner ContextVM event when one is present.
preconditions: An encrypted notification request has been published.
The result subscription is active.
steps: Deliver non-matching encrypted events with wrong `#e`, wrong `#p`, or a spoofed author.
Deliver the correctly correlated encrypted result event.
criteria.expected_result: Non-matching events are ignored, the correctly correlated event resolves the request, and the subscription is cleaned up after terminal resolution.
negative_cases: If a spoofed author can resolve the request, the criterion fails.
If duplicate correlated events trigger duplicate resolution or leave the subscription open, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Notification channel listing populates canonical channel state through encrypted transport
criteria.assertion: Loading the notifications list executes the `notifications.channels.list` encrypted operation, stores the returned channel array in `notificationState.channels`, clears prior channel errors, and turns off the loading indicator when the request completes.
preconditions: The requester can access `/notifications`.
Encrypted request discovery and signer requirements are satisfied.
steps: Load the notifications list route or call `listNotificationChannels()` directly.
Allow a successful correlated encrypted result to return one or more channels.
criteria.expected_result: The page renders the notifications heading and returned channels, `channelsLoading` becomes false, and `channelsError` is null after success.
negative_cases: If the route falls back to REST for the current first-party store path, the criterion fails.
If successful results do not replace the in-memory channel list, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: The returned channel name and destination are visible in the table.

criteria.title: Notification channel mutations remain on encrypted operations and update local channel state deterministically
criteria.assertion: Creating, updating, testing, and deleting notification channels use only the encrypted operations `notifications.channels.create`, `notifications.channels.update`, `notifications.channels.test`, and `notifications.channels.delete`; create and update upsert the returned channel by id, and delete removes the deleted id from local channel state.
preconditions: Encrypted request discovery and signer requirements are satisfied.
The notifications UI or store is able to invoke channel mutation actions.
steps: Create a new channel through the notifications form or store.
Update an existing channel.
Send a test notification for that channel.
Delete the channel.
criteria.expected_result: Only encrypted notification operations are invoked, created and updated channel payloads are reflected in local state, and deletion removes the channel from local state after a successful result.
negative_cases: If create, update, test, or delete uses a direct REST channel endpoint in the current store path, the criterion fails.
If update creates duplicate local rows instead of upserting by id, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: Successful create shows a success toast and returns to `/notifications`.
Successful test shows a success toast naming the channel.
Successful delete removes the row from the channel table.

criteria.title: Encrypted notification logs are loaded only through the encrypted logs operation
criteria.assertion: Retrieving notification delivery logs executes only `notifications.logs.list`, stores the returned entries in `notificationState.logs`, and sets `logsLoading` and `logsError` consistently around success and failure.
preconditions: Encrypted request discovery and signer requirements are satisfied.
steps: Invoke `listNotificationLogs()` with optional query parameters.
Observe store state before and after the encrypted result resolves.
criteria.expected_result: The logs request uses the encrypted logs operation, successful results populate `notificationState.logs`, and failures clear logs and populate `logsError`.
negative_cases: If delivery logs are fetched through a REST log endpoint in the current store path, the criterion fails.
If log failures leave stale log entries visible in `notificationState.logs`, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: The notifications log route can render encrypted-log results returned by the store.

criteria.title: Backend decrypt failures and unauthorized requests return terminal encrypted errors without dispatch
criteria.assertion: If an encrypted notification request cannot be decrypted or the requester pubkey is unauthorized for the targeted encrypted domain, Bahia publishes a correlated encrypted terminal error result and does not invoke the domain handler.
preconditions: The backend encrypted transport is subscribed to encrypted request events.
A malformed or unauthorized notification request is delivered.
steps: Send an undecryptable encrypted notification request, or send a decryptable request from an unauthorized pubkey.
Observe the backend encrypted result and handler behavior.
criteria.expected_result: A correlated terminal error result is published with an error code/message, and the protected notification handler path is not executed for the rejected request.
negative_cases: If the backend silently drops decrypt failures without a terminal result, the criterion fails.
If unauthorized requests reach the notification handler, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: Frontend callers surface the terminal error instead of proceeding as if the operation succeeded.

criteria.title: Terminal encrypted errors are surfaced to users without losing valid entered data
criteria.assertion: When an encrypted notification create or update action fails after the user has entered valid data, the route shows a visible error message and leaves the current form field values intact so the user can correct or retry without re-entering valid inputs.
preconditions: The notification create or edit form is open.
The user has entered syntactically valid form data.
steps: Submit the form.
Return a terminal encrypted error from the store path.
criteria.expected_result: A visible error is rendered in the form error region and the previously entered values remain in the form controls.
negative_cases: If form submission failure clears valid fields, the criterion fails.
If the user receives no visible error signal after an encrypted terminal error, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: The route-specific `saveError` is passed back into the form component after failed submit.

criteria.title: Notifications routes expose labelled controls and alert regions for browser assistive technologies
criteria.assertion: The notifications list and create flows expose semantic headings, form labels, and alert/status regions needed for browser-level automation and assistive technology to understand the page structure and error state.
preconditions: The user can access `/notifications` or `/notifications/new`.
steps: Load the notifications list route.
Load the create-notification route.
Trigger a form error in the channel form.
criteria.expected_result: The list route exposes a top-level `Notifications` heading and labelled filter controls; the form route exposes a top-level `Create notification channel` heading, labelled required inputs, and an error container with `role=alert` when submission fails.
negative_cases: If key filter or form controls are rendered without labels, the criterion fails.
If form submission errors are not exposed via an alert region, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Notifications browser journey stays on encrypted relays and off public relays end to end
criteria.assertion: In the first-party notifications browser journey, encrypted request publication and correlated result handling use only encrypted-request relays; the same journey must not publish sensitive notification payloads to public browser relays.
preconditions: System discovery advertises both public and encrypted relay URLs.
The user is authenticated with a signer that supports encryption.
steps: Load `/notifications`.
Create a notification channel.
Send a test notification.
Inspect the browser transport trace for publish relays and operations.
criteria.expected_result: The trace contains encrypted notification operations such as `notifications.channels.list`, `notifications.channels.create`, and `notifications.channels.test`; every corresponding publish relay is an encrypted-request relay URL and none is a public browser relay URL.
negative_cases: If the browser publishes notification requests to a public relay URL, the criterion fails.
If the encrypted browser journey still depends on a REST compatibility override, the criterion fails.

ui_signals: The notifications table shows the existing and newly created channels.
A success toast confirms the test notification was sent.

coverage_notes: These criteria are grounded in the current signer-first encrypted notifications implementation and existing browser/unit evidence, not the legacy REST compatibility client.
No quantified performance budget is currently specified in the selected source evidence, so no explicit performance acceptance criterion is asserted here.
Observability fields are intentionally sparse where the implementation exposes user-visible state changes but no explicit log or metric contract in the selected evidence.
unresolved_questions: Should encrypted-domain browser E2E breadth be expanded beyond list/create/test to require explicit edit/delete/log browser journeys as release-gating evidence?
